title: Reasoning models usually inherited the revision marker “wait” before reinforcement learning
summary: In 17 of 18 tested reinforcement-learning runs starting from models that rarely wrote “wait,” the word stayed rare even as math accuracy improved. In the traced OLMo-3 lineage, the word appeared during mid-training before reinforcement learning and became more frequent afterward.
organization: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Huawei Noah’s Ark Lab; Peking University

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 affiliations, main provenance contrasts, released-checkpoint lineage and robustness appendix

evidence.tested: The analysis compared published checkpoint histories and controlled training runs, using fewer than 0.05 occurrences per thousand generated tokens as its absence criterion.
evidence.unknown: The result concerns a visible marker on the sampled tasks. It does not show whether a model reconsidered an answer without writing “wait.”
evidence.ai_role: Researchers sampled language-model outputs across recorded training stages and externally released and newly trained reinforcement-learning checkpoints.
